lead.text: Scholars read the writing inside a sealed ancient scroll without opening it.
A lab measured a protein that an AI model had predicted, and the shape matched.
A publisher pulled many papers with undisclosed AI text, and a research council made its AI rule final.

new_findings.title: SAMPLE: A sealed scroll is read without being opened

explainer.found: A team at Eastvale University read about 1,800 Greek letters inside a papyrus scroll that cannot be unrolled. The scroll came from the library at Herculaneum. The letters fill six columns of text, and the passage is part of a prose work on friendship.
explainer.matters: Hundreds of scrolls from the same library are still sealed. A method that reads them without opening them leaves each scroll whole. Scholars could then study many scrolls, not only this one. One expert calls it the first whole passage of connected prose from a sealed scroll.
explainer.ai_helped: Eastvale University built a model called the Ink Reader. The team scanned the scroll with X-rays and flattened its layers in software, a step called virtual unwrapping. The Ink Reader, trained on small patches where ink had been found by hand, then marked the ink in the scans. People read the marked letters.
explainer.how_sure: Checked. Nature published the paper after peer review. Scholars in two countries, outside the Eastvale team, checked the readings. Two experts quoted here, at Ravenhurst University and the Coldwater Institute, call the readings careful.
explainer.background: Mount Vesuvius erupted in AD 79 and buried the Roman town of Herculaneum. The eruption charred hundreds of papyrus scrolls in its library. None of them can be unrolled.
explainer.could_lead: The same method could open other sealed scrolls and bring back books that no one has read since the eruption. Scholars may then learn what the library held.

new_findings.title: SAMPLE: A lab measures a protein that an AI had predicted

explainer.found: A second lab measured the shape of a protein complex and found that an AI model had predicted it correctly.
explainer.matters: A protein's shape shows how it works and how a drug might fit. Measuring a shape is slow.
explainer.ai_helped: Halden Research built the model, Halden Fold. It posted its prediction before anyone had measured the complex.
explainer.how_sure: Confirmed. PNAS published the measured structure, which matches the prediction in every chain. Halden Research did not do the measurement.
explainer.background: The lab used cryo-electron microscopy, which images frozen molecules, to measure the complex. A first safety trial of a drug that binds the complex is registered as NCT09999002.
explainer.could_lead: If more predictions match, AI could shorten the search for new medicines.

new_findings.title: SAMPLE: Example Press retracts 84 papers with undisclosed AI text

explainer.found: Example Press retracted 84 papers in nine journals. The text and images in these papers came from an AI tool that the authors did not disclose.
explainer.matters: Other researchers may have cited these papers, so the harm can spread beyond the journals.
explainer.ai_helped: An AI tool made the text and images. The publisher's notices do not name the tool.
explainer.how_sure: Checked. Example Press, the publisher of the papers, says so in its own statement and in two retraction notices.
explainer.background: A retraction notice tells readers that a paper should no longer be relied on.
explainer.could_lead: Publishers could check for undisclosed AI text before they accept a paper.

new_findings.title: SAMPLE: An AI lab claims a proof of an open problem

explainer.found: Marlow Labs says its AI system found a proof of an open problem about sums of sets of whole numbers.
explainer.matters: A proof would settle a question that mathematicians had left open.
explainer.ai_helped: Marlow Labs built the Marlow Prover. The lab says the system found the proof with no human step in the argument.
explainer.how_sure: Preprint. arXiv hosts the paper, which has not been peer reviewed. Marlow Labs is the source of the claim.
explainer.background: A Lean file posted with the paper lets a proof assistant check the argument by machine.
explainer.could_lead: If the Lean file checks, the proof could be accepted without waiting long for referees.

evidence.quote: The proof was found by the Marlow Prover with no human step in the argument

returning.update: The council published its final rule. From 1 January, applicants must say if AI tools helped write any part of a proposal. The final rule covers every part of a proposal, not only the summary.

rung.note: An independent lab repeated the work and got a matching result.

ideas.text: Oren Nominal (SAMPLE) argues that journals should let AI check every submitted proof before human review begins.
Sana Provisional (SAMPLE) argues that reviewers should be told plainly what they may share with AI tools.

corrections.after: A tiling covers a surface with copies of shapes and leaves no gaps. A floor of square tiles repeats one pattern. This proof is about tiles that never do that, on the flat plane only.
corrections.reason: The paper proves the result for the flat plane only. The first text did not say so, and a reader reported it.

corrections.after: Applied. The Meridian Weather Service says it runs the model alongside its own system and has not replaced that system. Science published the paper after peer review, and Larch Weather Systems, the maker, helped write it. The tests used past weather only, so live forecasts may differ.
corrections.reason: The weather service's statement says the model runs alongside its own system and has not replaced it. The first text said the service relies on the model.

report_decisions.reason: The paper proves the result for the plane only. The first text did not say so, so we wrote a clarification.
